sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit review factors
sections.summary: SkillsFuture Credit, introduced in January last year, is being reviewed using utilisation rate, fiscal position, training types and participation rate.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: SkillsFuture Credit, which was introduced in January last year, is part of this overall movement.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: Key factors, such as utilisation rate and the Government's fiscal position, are part of our review for the next tranche of SkillsFuture Credit.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: In addition, we are also considering broader trends, such as the types of training that Singaporeans are using their Credits for, and the training participation rate for Singaporeans.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit usage and outreach
sections.summary: 12 months after the $500 SkillsFuture Credit, 126,000 Singaporeans (5%) used credits for courses, and SSG plans SkillsFuture Engage outreach with five CDCs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Members will recall that, in a recent update as at end-2016, 12 months after we introduced the $500 SkillsFuture Credit, 126,000 Singaporeans, that means 5% of Singaporeans, have already used their credits to take up courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We are now focused on outreach, which is why SSG is currently planning a major outreach exercise called SkillsFuture Engage where SSG will work very closely with the five Community Development Councils to help Singaporeans navigate the training landscape, the SkillsFuture credit directory and so on.

sections.label: Employer subsidies for worker training
sections.summary: Besides the $500 SkillsFuture Credit, schemes help employers develop workers, with subsidies up to 50% or 90% of course fees for SSG-supported courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Allow me to reassure Mr Patrick Tay and Members that in addition to the SkillsFuture Credit of $500, we have also put in place different schemes to assist and encourage employers to develop their workers, especially older workers and low-income workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: If we recall, based on this scheme, the employers are eligible for subsidies ranging from up to 50% or even up to 90% of the course fees for SSG-supported courses.
